cards.definition: A structural equation encodes a behavioral or causal relationship under specified invariance assumptions, whereas a reduced form expresses observables in terms of exogenous inputs and disturbances after solving the system. A reduced-form coefficient need not equal a single structural causal parameter.
major_error_concepts: Treating any predictive regression coefficient as invariant to a policy intervention.
cards.prompt: What is Structural and Reduced Form Models? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Behavioral structure differs from solved observable relationships.

cards.definition: A population moment condition restricts an expectation, such as E[g(W,theta0)]=0 at the target parameter. It may encode orthogonality, likelihood implications, or economic restrictions; its validity is an assumption about the population process.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a sample moment near zero proves the population restriction economically valid.
cards.prompt: What is Population Moment Condition? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Expectation restriction holding at the intended parameter.

accepted_variants: Sample analog of an expectation restriction.
cards.definition: A sample moment averages a moment function over observed data, gbar(theta)=n^(-1) sum g(Wi,theta). Under appropriate sampling and uniform convergence conditions it approximates its population counterpart, not necessarily exactly in a finite sample.
major_error_concepts: Equating finite-sample moments exactly to population expectations by definition.
cards.prompt: What is Sample Moment? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Empirical average approximating a population moment under conditions.

cards.definition: The method of moments estimates parameters by matching empirical and model-implied moments. With as many independent identifying equations as parameters, a just-identified solution may set all sample moments to zero; existence and uniqueness still require conditions.
major_error_concepts: Assuming equal numbers of moments and parameters guarantee unique identification.
cards.prompt: What is Method of Moments? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Parameter estimates solve or match identifying sample moments.

accepted_variants: GMM objective with a positive-definite appropriate weight matrix.
cards.definition: Generalized method of moments minimizes a weighted quadratic form in sample moment discrepancies. GMM can accommodate more moments than parameters, and its consistency depends on valid moments, identification, and regularity rather than the minimization algorithm alone.
major_error_concepts: Calling a numerical minimum proof that the moment assumptions are true.
cards.prompt: What is Generalized Method of Moments? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Minimize gbar(theta)prime W gbar(theta) using valid identifying moments.

cards.definition: A GMM weighting matrix specifies the relative emphasis and covariance adjustment applied to moment discrepancies. Its choice affects efficiency and finite-sample behavior, while valid identification can permit consistency under many suitable positive-definite limits.
major_error_concepts: Assuming only the efficient weight matrix can yield any consistent GMM estimator.
cards.prompt: What is GMM Weighting Matrix? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Weights determine how moment discrepancies are combined.

accepted_variants: Full-rank derivative of expected moments near the target.
cards.definition: Local moment identification requires parameter changes to produce distinguishable changes in population moments near the target. A full-column-rank moment Jacobian is a standard local condition under regularity, but it is not by itself a global uniqueness guarantee.
major_error_concepts: Confusing local Jacobian rank with global identification across all parameter values.
cards.prompt: What is Moment Identification Rank? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Moment sensitivity has sufficient local rank to distinguish parameters.

cards.definition: Efficient GMM uses the inverse of the asymptotic covariance matrix of the sample moments as its weighting limit. The covariance must reflect heteroskedasticity or dependence as appropriate; efficiency is relative to the chosen valid moment set.
major_error_concepts: Ignoring serial or cluster dependence when estimating the moment covariance.
cards.prompt: What is Efficient GMM? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Inverse long-run moment covariance yields efficient weighting under conditions.

cards.definition: Two-step GMM first obtains a consistent preliminary estimate, estimates the moment covariance at that estimate, and then re-estimates with an efficient weight. Estimated weights can affect small-sample inference, especially in complex panel applications.
major_error_concepts: Assuming first-step and second-step standard errors are automatically interchangeable.
cards.prompt: What is Two Step GMM? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Initial fit supplies covariance weights for a second GMM fit.

accepted_variants: Hansen J test with compatible covariance assumptions.
cards.definition: A GMM overidentification test uses the minimized appropriately weighted moment discrepancy to test whether extra moment restrictions jointly fit. Its usual chi-squared reference requires the maintained regularity and identification conditions, and non-rejection does not prove every instrument valid.
major_error_concepts: Treating a high J-test p-value as proof of all exclusion restrictions.
cards.prompt: What is Overidentification Test? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Joint test of excess moment restrictions under a maintained identified model.

accepted_variants: Exact identification versus excess identifying restrictions.
cards.definition: A model is just identified when independent valid identifying restrictions match the parameter dimension; it is overidentified when additional restrictions remain. In a just-identified moment model, no excess moments remain for a conventional overidentification test.
major_error_concepts: Assuming an overidentification test exists in every single-instrument single-treatment model.
cards.prompt: What is Just and Overidentified Models? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Restriction count and independence distinguish just from overidentification.

accepted_variants: Extremum estimator based on an averaged objective.
cards.definition: An M-estimator optimizes an empirical average of a criterion function, covering estimators such as least squares and maximum likelihood. Its statistical target is defined by the population criterion, which may differ from an intended causal quantity if the model is misspecified.
major_error_concepts: Assuming any optimized criterion automatically targets the desired causal parameter.
cards.prompt: What is M Estimation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Empirical criterion optimization defines a broad estimator class.

cards.definition: Consistency of an extremum estimator typically requires the sample objective to converge suitably to a population objective with a uniquely identified optimum, together with compactness or other control of parameter behavior. Pointwise convergence alone may be insufficient for convergence of optimizers.
major_error_concepts: Inferring estimator consistency solely from convergence of one objective value.
cards.prompt: What is Extremum Estimator Consistency? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Uniform or adequate objective convergence plus a uniquely identified target and regularity.

accepted_variants: Root-n normal approximation for a regular estimator.
cards.definition: Asymptotic normality of a regular estimator often follows from a local expansion of its estimating equations and a central limit theorem. Boundary parameters, weak identification, nonsmooth criteria, or dependence can change the rate or limiting distribution.
major_error_concepts: Applying root-n normal inference automatically at a parameter boundary or weakly identified point.
cards.prompt: What is Asymptotic Normality? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Local linearization and a CLT produce normal limits only under qualifying regularity.

accepted_variants: For a scalar differentiable transformation, the limiting variance is [g'(theta0)] squared times V under the underlying root-n normal limit.
cards.definition: If sqrt(n)*(thetaHat-theta0) converges in distribution to N(0,V) and g is differentiable at theta0, then sqrt(n)*(g(thetaHat)-g(theta0)) converges to N(0,G V G transpose), with G the derivative matrix of g there. A zero derivative gives a degenerate first-order limit; a useful nondegenerate approximation then may require a higher-order expansion and different rate.
major_error_concepts: Applying the unchanged covariance V to an arbitrary nonlinear transformation.
Concluding a zero first derivative means the transformed estimate has exactly zero finite-sample uncertainty.
cards.prompt: What is Delta Method? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Use the derivative of the transformation at the target to propagate the estimator's asymptotic covariance: G V G transpose.
Differentiability and the underlying normal limit are hypotheses; a vanishing derivative may require a higher-order approximation for nondegenerate inference.

cards.definition: A sandwich covariance combines the sensitivity of estimating equations with the covariance of their random variation. In schematic form it is A inverse times B times A inverse transpose, with scaling and dependence treatment matched to the estimator.
major_error_concepts: Assuming sandwich covariance corrects an inconsistent point estimator.
cards.prompt: What is Sandwich Covariance? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Sensitivity and score or moment variation jointly determine robust asymptotic covariance.

cards.definition: Maximum likelihood estimates parameters by maximizing the probability density or mass assigned to observed data under a specified statistical model. Correct specification and regularity support familiar efficiency and inference results; a large likelihood value alone is not evidence of causal identification.
major_error_concepts: Treating likelihood as the probability the parameter is true without a prior.
cards.prompt: What is Maximum Likelihood Estimation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Optimize the joint data likelihood under a specified model.

cards.definition: The score is the gradient of the log likelihood with respect to parameters. Under regularity and correct specification its expectation is zero at the truth, making it an estimating function; realized scores need not vanish away from an interior optimum.
major_error_concepts: Confusing the score with the likelihood level itself.
cards.prompt: What is Likelihood Score? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Parameter derivative of log likelihood.

cards.definition: Fisher information measures expected likelihood curvature or score variation under conditions making those expressions agree. It describes local statistical information about parameters, not causal credibility of the model's economic interpretation.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the information equality holds unchanged under arbitrary misspecification.
cards.prompt: What is Fisher Information? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Expected score covariance equals negative expected log-likelihood Hessian under regularity.

cards.definition: Quasi-maximum likelihood optimizes a chosen likelihood-like criterion even when the full distributional model is not asserted correct. It can consistently estimate some parameters under weaker conditions, such as a correctly specified conditional mean, but those conditions and robust covariance must be stated.
major_error_concepts: Claiming every misspecified likelihood remains consistent for the intended parameter.
cards.prompt: What is Quasi Maximum Likelihood? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Likelihood criterion may target parameters under weaker moment restrictions than full distributional correctness.

cards.definition: Under misspecification, an estimator may converge to a pseudo-true parameter that optimizes its population criterion within the chosen model class. This is a well-defined approximation target but need not equal the structural or causal parameter originally desired.
major_error_concepts: Calling convergence to any stable parameter proof of causal correctness.
cards.prompt: What is Pseudo True Parameter? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Best criterion-based approximation within a misspecified model need not be the substantive target.

cards.definition: A Wald test measures how far unrestricted parameter estimates violate null restrictions relative to their estimated covariance. Nonlinear restrictions require suitable derivatives, and finite-sample results can depend on equivalent parameterizations of the same null.
major_error_concepts: Assuming all nonlinear reparameterizations give identical finite-sample Wald statistics.
cards.prompt: What is Wald Test? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Standardized restriction discrepancy evaluated at the unrestricted estimator.

cards.definition: A score or Lagrange-multiplier test evaluates whether the criterion's gradient at the restricted fit points strongly toward improving fit outside the null. It often avoids fitting the unrestricted model, but its reference distribution still relies on regularity and identification.
major_error_concepts: Confusing a score test with the size of unrestricted coefficients.
cards.prompt: What is Score Test? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Use restricted-fit score information to test excluded directions.

cards.definition: A likelihood-ratio test compares maximized log likelihoods under restricted and unrestricted nested models. Its usual chi-squared approximation can fail with boundary parameters, unidentified nuisance parameters, or nonstandard sampling conditions.
major_error_concepts: Applying the ordinary chi-squared rule to every boundary or mixture-model test.
cards.prompt: What is Likelihood Ratio Test? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Twice the log-likelihood improvement from relaxing nested restrictions.

cards.definition: The bootstrap approximates an estimator's sampling behavior by repeatedly resampling or simulating according to a scheme justified for the problem. Resampling must preserve the relevant design or dependence; it is not a universal repair for weak identification, selection bias, or nonregular estimators.
major_error_concepts: Assuming any estimator becomes valid by adding bootstrap standard errors.
cards.prompt: What is Bootstrap? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Resampling-based approximation with a task-appropriate sampling scheme.

cards.definition: A pairs bootstrap resamples entire observation vectors, preserving each row's regressor-outcome pairing. It is natural for qualifying IID random-design settings; resampling X and Y independently would destroy the relationship being estimated.
major_error_concepts: Resampling regressors and outcomes separately as if they were unrelated margins.
cards.prompt: What is Pairs Bootstrap? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Resample paired observation vectors together under appropriate IID conditions.

cards.definition: A wild bootstrap generates artificial errors by multiplying fitted residuals by suitable random weights, often to accommodate heteroskedasticity. Residual adjustments, null imposition, and weight choice affect validity in the intended regression test.
major_error_concepts: Treating simple identical-variance residual resampling as equivalent under arbitrary heteroskedasticity.
cards.prompt: What is Wild Bootstrap? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Randomly reweight residuals to reproduce heteroskedastic sampling variation under conditions.

accepted_variants: Cluster pairs or wild-cluster bootstrap with scheme specified.
cards.definition: A cluster bootstrap resamples or reweights whole clusters to preserve within-cluster dependence. Validity depends on the cluster design and asymptotic regime; many rows inside a few clusters do not automatically supply reliable cluster-level inference.
major_error_concepts: Breaking clusters into independent rows while claiming clustered dependence is preserved.
cards.prompt: What is Cluster Bootstrap? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Resampling respects independent cluster units rather than individual dependent rows.

accepted_variants: Moving-block or stationary bootstrap under its stated construction.
cards.definition: A block bootstrap resamples contiguous or otherwise structured blocks to retain local dependence in time-series data. Block length trades off captured dependence and effective resampling variation, and stationarity or other method-specific assumptions remain necessary.
major_error_concepts: Randomly resampling individual dates and claiming all serial dependence is retained.
cards.prompt: What is Block Bootstrap? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Block resampling preserves qualifying serial dependence.

accepted_variants: Design-based permutation inference under valid assignments.
cards.definition: Randomization inference compares a statistic with its distribution over assignments allowed by the actual randomization design. Exact imputation under a sharp null is a common case; testing an average-effect null generally needs additional treatment and assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Permuting labels arbitrarily without respecting blocked or clustered assignment.
cards.prompt: What is Randomization Inference? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Reference distribution derives from the assignment mechanism and the specific null.

accepted_variants: Partialling out controls in linear IV.
cards.definition: With included exogenous controls, instrumental-variable identification uses the instrument's variation remaining after accounting for those controls. Residualizing the outcome, endogenous regressor, and excluded instrument consistently clarifies the partial first-stage and reduced-form relationships.
major_error_concepts: Checking only the raw instrument-treatment correlation when controls absorb that variation.
cards.prompt: What is Partialling Out in IV? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Conditional IV uses consistently partialled-out instrument and regressor variation.

cards.definition: In linear IV notation, 2SLS is betaHat=(Xprime Pz X)^(-1)Xprime Pz Y when the required matrices have rank, with Pz the projection onto the instrument space. All included exogenous regressors belong in the instrument set, and inference uses the structural residuals appropriately.
major_error_concepts: Omitting included exogenous controls from the instrument set without a justified alternative.
cards.prompt: What is Matrix Two Stage Least Squares? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Project regressors onto the full instrument space and solve the IV least-squares equations.

cards.definition: Limited-information maximum likelihood estimates a structural equation using the information and instrument restrictions for that equation. It can have different finite-sample behavior from 2SLS, especially with many instruments, but is not immune to invalid instruments or weak identification.
major_error_concepts: Claiming LIML makes exclusion violations irrelevant.
cards.prompt: What is Limited Information Maximum Likelihood? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Equation-level likelihood-based IV estimator with its own sampling properties.

accepted_variants: Weak-instrument identification as an important case.
cards.definition: Weak identification occurs when the observable implications change too little with key parameter changes for standard asymptotics to be reliable. In IV this often corresponds to weak first-stage instruments; diagnostic thresholds depend on design and inference objectives rather than one universal rule.
major_error_concepts: Declaring all IV designs strong from one threshold regardless of heteroskedasticity or instrument count.
cards.prompt: What is Weak Identification? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Low parameter sensitivity undermines conventional approximations.

accepted_variants: AR test with appropriate robust implementation.
cards.definition: An Anderson-Rubin test evaluates a hypothesized structural coefficient by testing instrument restrictions in the transformed outcome Y-betaNull*X, with nuisance handling specified. Under its maintained instrument validity and error assumptions, it can remain valid even when the first stage is weak.
major_error_concepts: Assuming weak-IV robustness also protects against an invalid exclusion restriction.
cards.prompt: What is Anderson Rubin Test? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Test the structural null through transformed-outcome instrument moments without dividing by a weak first stage.

cards.definition: A weak-identification-robust confidence set can be formed by inverting tests valid under weak identification. It may be wide, disconnected, or unbounded, honestly reflecting limited information rather than necessarily a software error.
major_error_concepts: Forcing every weak-IV confidence set into a narrow symmetric interval.
cards.prompt: What is Weak Identification Robust Confidence Set? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Invert valid weak-identification tests; unusual set shapes can be informative.

cards.definition: Many-instrument problems arise when a large instrument set overfits endogenous regressors or distorts covariance and testing approximations. Instrument count relative to independent information matters, and adding instruments can worsen finite-sample performance despite extra nominal moment restrictions.
major_error_concepts: Assuming more instruments always improve an IV estimate.
cards.prompt: What is Many Instruments? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Instrument proliferation can harm estimation and inference.

cards.definition: With heterogeneous treatment effects, an IV coefficient generally aggregates effects using the variation induced by the instrument and the model's weighting structure. It need not equal an unweighted population average, and the weights can be complicated outside the binary monotonic case.
major_error_concepts: Calling every IV coefficient the population ATE.
cards.prompt: What is Heterogeneous Treatment Effects in IV? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: IV targets an instrument- and design-dependent effect under heterogeneity.

cards.definition: In the binary instrument-treatment setting, LATE is the average treatment effect among compliers under independence, exclusion, relevance, and monotonicity. It is local to people whose treatment receipt changes with the instrument, not automatically to all treated units.
major_error_concepts: Equating compliers with everyone observed receiving treatment.
cards.prompt: What is Local Average Treatment Effect? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Average effect for instrument-induced compliers under the defining assumptions.

cards.definition: IV monotonicity requires that changing the binary instrument in its treatment-encouraging direction does not reduce treatment for any unit. It rules out defiers for that instrument contrast, without requiring equal treatment effects or universal compliance.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting monotonicity as a constant treatment effect assumption.
cards.prompt: What is IV Monotonicity? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: No unit moves treatment in the opposite direction to the monotone encouragement.

cards.definition: Compliance types describe a unit's treatment receipt under each possible assignment: always-takers, never-takers, compliers, or defiers in the binary case. Type is defined by two potential receipt states, so it is usually not fully observed for an individual.
major_error_concepts: Identifying every individual's type solely from one observed assignment and receipt.
cards.prompt: What is Compliance Types? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Latent receipt responses to both assignment states define compliance type.

cards.definition: A causal IV exclusion restriction says assignment or instrument affects the outcome only through the specified received treatment. Information, expectations, other services, or direct incentives caused by the instrument can violate this channel restriction even when assignment is randomized.
major_error_concepts: Assuming randomizing an encouragement proves it has no direct outcome channel.
cards.prompt: What is Causal IV Exclusion? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: No outcome effect outside the defined treatment pathway.

cards.definition: Transporting an IV effect to another population requires assumptions connecting its complier effects, treatment margins, and context to the new target. Different instruments can identify different local effects without either estimate being statistically incorrect.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting different instrument estimates automatically as evidence one is invalid despite heterogeneous compliers.
cards.prompt: What is Transportability of IV Effects? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Local IV effects need additional assumptions for broader or different-population claims.

accepted_variants: Residual-inclusion method when the required control representation holds.
cards.definition: A control-function approach includes a constructed term capturing endogenous selection or dependence, often from a first-stage model. Its validity relies on explicit distributional or structural assumptions and is not guaranteed simply by adding any fitted residual to a regression.
major_error_concepts: Treating residual inclusion as universally equivalent to valid IV in nonlinear models.
cards.prompt: What is Control Function? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Model-based control accounts for endogenous dependence under specified assumptions.

cards.definition: A simultaneous-equations model specifies multiple endogenous variables determined jointly, such as supply and demand setting price and quantity. Identification of individual structural equations needs restrictions that distinguish their shifts rather than a single observed equilibrium correlation.
major_error_concepts: Reading a supply or demand slope directly from an unrestricted price-quantity correlation.
cards.prompt: What is Simultaneous Equations? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Jointly determined endogenous variables require equation-specific identifying variation.

accepted_variants: Order condition for linear structural-equation identification.
cards.definition: An order condition counts excluded exogenous variables relative to included endogenous regressors in a simultaneous equation. Having enough exclusions is generally necessary in the standard linear setup but not sufficient for identification because their actual rank and validity matter.
major_error_concepts: Claiming the equation is identified solely because the exclusion counts match.
cards.prompt: What is Order Condition for Identification? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Restriction count is a necessary screening condition, not a sufficient rank test.

accepted_variants: Instrument relevance matrix has the needed rank.
cards.definition: The rank condition requires excluded exogenous variation to move the relevant endogenous regressors in sufficiently independent directions. It checks the substantive linear independence missing from a restriction count, conditional on the structural model and valid exclusions.
major_error_concepts: Assuming multiple duplicate instruments identify multiple endogenous effects independently.
cards.prompt: What is Simultaneous Equation Rank Condition? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Excluded variation spans the required endogenous directions.

cards.definition: Validation data measure a more credible version of an error-prone variable for some observations. They can inform measurement-error correction when the validation process and relation to the main sample are modeled appropriately; a validation label alone does not remove selection or reference error.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a selected validation sample automatically generalizes without adjustment.
cards.prompt: What is Measurement Validation Data? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Additional credible measurements identify aspects of the measurement process under assumptions.

cards.definition: An instrument for an error-prone regressor must predict its true component while remaining appropriately unrelated to the structural error and measurement error. A second measurement can sometimes serve, but correlated measurement errors can invalidate that strategy.
major_error_concepts: Assuming any duplicate measurement is valid even when both share the same reporting error.
cards.prompt: What is IV for Measurement Error? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: IV correction needs correlation with true signal and suitable error orthogonality.

cards.definition: Censoring records observations with outcomes known only within a boundary category, while truncation excludes observations outside the selection range entirely. Their likelihoods and target populations differ, so they cannot generally be analyzed by the same ordinary outcome regression.
major_error_concepts: Treating all excluded or top-coded values as the same observation mechanism.
cards.prompt: What is Censoring and Truncation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Limited observed outcome value differs from absent units due to outcome-based selection.

accepted_variants: Type I Tobit under stated homoskedastic normal assumptions.
cards.definition: A standard Tobit model combines a latent linear normal outcome with an observed censoring rule. Its coefficient concerns the latent index; effects on the observed mean and on the probability of being uncensored require different transformations and depend on the model assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Using Tobit for every zero-heavy outcome without justifying a censored latent process.
cards.prompt: What is Tobit Model? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Latent-outcome model plus censoring; coefficients are not automatically observed-mean effects.

accepted_variants: Heckman sample-selection model or two-step correction.
cards.definition: A Heckman selection model jointly describes observation selection and a latent outcome, often using a bivariate-normal error structure. A credible exclusion in the selection equation can strengthen identification beyond functional-form assumptions, and arbitrary missingness does not automatically fit this model.
major_error_concepts: Claiming the correction solves any missing-data problem without a selection model.
cards.prompt: What is Heckman Selection Model? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Joint selection-outcome structure corrects selection under strong specified assumptions.

accepted_variants: lambda(z)=phi(z)/Phi(z) for the corresponding upper selection convention.
cards.definition: An inverse Mills ratio is a normal density-to-tail-probability ratio arising in expectations under truncated normal selection. In a specified Heckman model it becomes a selection-control term; its sign and denominator depend on which selection event is modeled.
major_error_concepts: Using a fixed sign and tail without checking the selection rule.
cards.prompt: What is Inverse Mills Ratio? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Normal density-tail ratio captures a model-specific truncated conditional mean.

accepted_variants: MAR under the stated observed-data set.
cards.definition: Missing at random means the probability of missingness can depend on observed information but not on the missing values after conditioning on that information. It is an assumption about the observation mechanism, not a claim that missing cases were selected by a randomized experiment.
major_error_concepts: Equating MAR with missing completely at random.
cards.prompt: What is Missing at Random? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Conditional missingness independence given observed data.

cards.definition: Inverse-probability weighting for missing outcomes reweights observed cases by the inverse of their modeled observation probability. Identification requires appropriate conditional missingness assumptions and positive observation chances; extreme weights can greatly reduce precision.
major_error_concepts: Assuming weights identify outcomes for groups with zero chance of observation.
cards.prompt: What is Missing Outcome Weighting? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Reweight observed cases using valid positive observation probabilities.

accepted_variants: MI with appropriate pooling of estimates and variances.
cards.definition: Multiple imputation creates several plausible completed datasets under a specified imputation model, analyzes each, and combines within- and between-imputation uncertainty. Its validity depends on missingness and model compatibility, not simply on filling every blank value.
major_error_concepts: Treating one deterministic filled dataset as accounting for all missing-data uncertainty.
cards.prompt: What is Multiple Imputation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Multiple draws and combined uncertainty under a justified imputation model.

accepted_variants: Selection on observables or conditional exchangeability.
cards.definition: Conditional unconfoundedness requires treatment assignment to be independent of potential outcomes given observed pre-treatment covariates. Together with overlap and consistency, it can identify treatment effects through adjustment, but unobserved confounding remains a substantive vulnerability.
major_error_concepts: Assuming including many controls proves all confounding has been removed.
cards.prompt: What is Conditional Unconfoundedness? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Potential outcomes independent of treatment conditional on the chosen pre-treatment covariates.

cards.definition: Overlap requires relevant treatment states to have positive probability at covariate values represented in the target population. Near-violations create unstable comparisons, while strict violations require extrapolation or a narrower target rather than purely data-supported adjustment.
major_error_concepts: Claiming matching recovers a comparison group where no comparable control can occur.
cards.prompt: What is Treatment Overlap? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Both treatment possibilities must occur with positive probability over target support.

accepted_variants: Balancing score under the defining assumptions.
cards.definition: The propensity score is the conditional probability of treatment given observed covariates. Under appropriate unconfoundedness, it can summarize balancing information for adjustment, but a fitted score's predictive performance does not establish absence of unmeasured confounding.
major_error_concepts: Calling a high treatment-prediction score proof of causal validity.
cards.prompt: What is Propensity Score? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: e(X)=P(D=1|X), a treatment-assignment probability.

accepted_variants: Covariate or propensity-score matching with target specified.
cards.definition: Matching constructs comparisons between treated and untreated observations with similar relevant covariates or balancing scores. It targets a specified population effect under identification and support assumptions; matching on observed variables cannot by itself remove unobserved confounding.
major_error_concepts: Assuming matched groups are causally comparable regardless of hidden differences.
cards.prompt: What is Treatment Effect Matching? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Construct comparable observed-covariate groups under overlap and exchangeability.

accepted_variants: IPW or propensity weighting with normalization convention stated.
cards.definition: Treatment inverse-probability weighting uses assignment probabilities to form a reweighted comparison targeting a defined effect. For an ATE, treated outcomes receive weights proportional to 1/e(X) and controls to 1/(1-e(X)); overlap and a valid assignment model remain essential.
major_error_concepts: Using ATE and treated-population weights interchangeably without changing the estimand.
cards.prompt: What is Treatment Inverse Probability Weighting? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Weight treatment groups by inverse assignment probabilities for the specified target.

accepted_variants: G-computation or regression standardization under stated assumptions.
cards.definition: Outcome regression adjustment estimates treatment-specific conditional outcome means and averages the relevant contrasts over the target covariate distribution. Its causal interpretation requires exchangeability, consistency, and support; a convenient outcome model alone does not supply identification.
major_error_concepts: Averaging over a different population while claiming the same target effect.
cards.prompt: What is Outcome Regression Standardization? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Model conditional potential-outcome means and standardize their contrast over the target.

accepted_variants: Augmented inverse-probability weighting with its double-robustness property.
cards.definition: A doubly robust treatment-effect estimator combines propensity and outcome models so that consistency can hold if either nuisance model is correct under the identification conditions. It is not robust to both being wrong, unmeasured confounding, or lack of overlap.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting doubly robust as immune to any two sources of bias.
cards.prompt: What is Doubly Robust Estimation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: One of two nuisance models can suffice for consistency under maintained causal assumptions.

cards.definition: Cross-fitting estimates nuisance functions on one data portion and evaluates estimating equations on another, rotating folds to use observations efficiently. It reduces overfitting dependence in qualifying semiparametric procedures, but folds must respect dependence and it does not cure identification failures.
major_error_concepts: Treating cross-fitting alone as proof of valid causal assumptions or adequate nuisance convergence.
cards.prompt: What is Cross Fitting? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Separate nuisance training and score evaluation through rotated splits.

cards.definition: Double or debiased machine learning combines orthogonal estimating scores with suitable nuisance estimation and often cross-fitting. Orthogonality reduces first-order sensitivity to nuisance error, but valid inference still needs identification, overlap where relevant, rate conditions, and compatible sampling.
major_error_concepts: Assuming using two prediction algorithms automatically yields a valid double-machine-learning estimator.
cards.prompt: What is Orthogonal Score Estimation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Orthogonal score plus controlled nuisance estimation supports target-parameter inference under conditions.

cards.definition: A bad control is a conditioning variable that changes or biases the intended causal contrast, such as a post-treatment mediator or a collider. Whether a control is appropriate depends on the causal question and structure, not merely on its correlation with the outcome.
major_error_concepts: Assuming adding every predictive covariate always reduces causal bias.
cards.prompt: What is Bad Controls? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Conditioning can harm identification depending on the variable's causal role.

cards.definition: A mediator lies on a causal path from treatment to outcome. Conditioning on it can remove part of the total effect and may introduce other biases; identifying direct or indirect effects requires additional assumptions beyond those identifying the total effect.
major_error_concepts: Calling a mediator-adjusted slope the total treatment effect without justification.
cards.prompt: What is Mediator Adjustment? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Intermediate causal variable changes the effect question when conditioned on.

cards.definition: A collider is a variable caused by two other variables along a path. Conditioning on a collider or certain descendants can induce association between its causes, opening a noncausal path that was previously blocked.
major_error_concepts: Treating a common effect as equivalent to a common-cause confounder.
cards.prompt: What is Collider Bias? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Conditioning on a common effect can create noncausal association.

accepted_variants: Causal robustness analysis with a stated sensitivity parameter.
cards.definition: Sensitivity analysis examines how conclusions change under specified departures from identifying or modeling assumptions. It must define the departure scale and interpretable range; stability across a few convenient regressions is not a complete analysis of unobserved confounding.
major_error_concepts: Claiming robustness to all hidden bias from a small set of similar specifications.
cards.prompt: What is Identification Sensitivity Analysis? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Quantify dependence of conclusions on explicit assumption violations.

cards.definition: Partial identification derives a set of parameter values consistent with the observations and maintained assumptions rather than a single point. Bounds can be informative; sharpness means every value in the proposed set is attainable under the model, not merely that the interval is narrow.
major_error_concepts: Equating a confidence interval around a point estimate with an identified set.
cards.prompt: What is Partial Identification? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Data and assumptions identify a set; sharpness concerns attainability.

cards.definition: The within transformation subtracts each unit's time mean to remove additive time-invariant unit effects in a linear panel model. Coefficients are identified from remaining within variation, so time-invariant regressors cannot be separately estimated by this transformation alone.
major_error_concepts: Claiming the within estimator separately identifies a constant unit attribute's slope.
cards.prompt: What is Within Transformation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Demeaning removes additive unit constants and uses within-unit variation.

cards.definition: Strict exogeneity in a panel requires a period's idiosyncratic error to have zero conditional mean given the unit's regressors across all modeled dates and its effect. Feedback from current shocks to future regressors can violate it even if contemporaneous regressors are uncorrelated with current errors.
major_error_concepts: Equating contemporaneous exogeneity with strict exogeneity.
cards.prompt: What is Panel Strict Exogeneity? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Error orthogonality extends to past, current, and future regressor history under the conditioning model.

cards.definition: First differencing removes a time-invariant additive unit effect by subtracting consecutive observations. Differenced errors can be serially correlated even when original errors are not, and differencing does not automatically solve endogenous regressor problems.
major_error_concepts: Assuming differenced observations are independent because original period errors were independent.
cards.prompt: What is First Difference Estimator? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Adjacent differences eliminate additive unit constants but change error dependence.

cards.definition: Random-effects GLS uses a modeled error-components covariance and restrictions linking unit effects to regressors. It can combine within and between variation efficiently under those restrictions, but unmodeled correlation between unit effects and regressors can cause inconsistency.
major_error_concepts: Claiming random effects remains consistent under arbitrary unit-effect correlation with regressors.
cards.prompt: What is Random Effects GLS? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: GLS exploits an error-components structure with required regressor-effect orthogonality.

accepted_variants: Mundlak or correlated-effects specification with unit means.
cards.definition: A correlated-random-effects model explicitly models association between unit effects and regressors, often by including unit means of time-varying covariates. A Mundlak-type specification can recover within-effect relationships under its linear assumptions while allowing additional between-unit structure.
major_error_concepts: Assuming adding unit means fixes every time-varying omitted confounder.
cards.prompt: What is Correlated Random Effects? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Model regressor-effect correlation rather than imposing independence.

accepted_variants: Hausman specification test with valid covariance of the difference.
cards.definition: A Hausman-type test compares estimators that should agree under a null but differ when one becomes inconsistent. Standard fixed-versus-random-effects implementations need appropriate covariance assumptions, and non-rejection does not prove the stronger random-effects restrictions true.
major_error_concepts: Treating a non-significant comparison as proof that random effects are exogenous.
cards.prompt: What is Hausman Test? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Estimator disagreement tests a specified consistency restriction.

cards.definition: Two-way fixed effects include unit and time effects, absorbing additive unit constants and shocks common to each date. Treatment coefficients still need an identification argument; with staggered adoption and heterogeneous effects, a single coefficient can combine problematic comparisons.
major_error_concepts: Claiming time fixed effects remove every differential group trend or heterogeneous treatment bias.
cards.prompt: What is Two Way Fixed Effects? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Unit and time additive effects do not alone guarantee a causal treatment coefficient.

accepted_variants: Unit, higher-level, or multiway cluster inference with assumptions specified.
cards.definition: Panel inference should account for within-unit dependence and any additional shared assignment or shock structure. Clustering by unit may be insufficient when treatment or disturbances are shared at a higher level, and two-way clustering requires its own adequate cluster asymptotics.
major_error_concepts: Assuming unit clustering handles every common regional or date-level shock.
cards.prompt: What is Panel Dependence and Clustering? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Choose dependence groups according to panel shocks and assignment, not row count.

cards.definition: A dynamic panel includes lagged outcomes or other predetermined variables among its regressors. Removing fixed effects can correlate transformed lagged outcomes with transformed errors, so ordinary static-panel exogeneity arguments may no longer apply.
major_error_concepts: Applying static strict-exogeneity results unchanged to a short panel with lagged dependent variables.
cards.prompt: What is Dynamic Panel Model? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Lagged outcomes interact with effect removal to create endogeneity concerns.

cards.definition: Nickell bias is the finite-time-dimension bias of the within estimator in standard dynamic panels with lagged outcomes and fixed effects. Increasing the number of units alone does not remove it when the number of periods remains fixed.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a very large cross section eliminates fixed-T dynamic-panel bias.
cards.prompt: What is Nickell Bias? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Dynamic within bias persists as N grows with fixed T.

cards.definition: Difference GMM for dynamic panels uses moment restrictions that can instrument differenced endogenous or predetermined regressors with suitable earlier levels. Lag validity depends on serial-correlation and timing assumptions; choosing every available lag without scrutiny can create weak or excessive instruments.
major_error_concepts: Treating all lagged levels as valid instruments regardless of error serial correlation.
cards.prompt: What is Difference GMM for Panels? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Earlier levels instrument differenced equations under explicit orthogonality restrictions.

cards.definition: System GMM combines differenced equations with level equations instrumented by suitable lagged differences. The additional level moments require extra restrictions, such as appropriate initial-condition relationships, and can fail even when difference-equation moments are valid.
major_error_concepts: Assuming adding level equations supplies valid instruments without new assumptions.
cards.prompt: What is System GMM for Panels? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Combine level and difference moments with additional identifying assumptions.

cards.definition: An event-study specification estimates outcome contrasts indexed by time relative to an event or treatment. The omitted reference period, comparison group, anticipation, treatment timing, and heterogeneity determine what the coefficients mean causally.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting any lead-lag plot as causal without identifying its counterfactual comparison.
cards.prompt: What is Event Study Design? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Relative-event-time coefficients require a defined baseline and valid comparisons.

cards.definition: Staggered adoption means different groups begin treatment at different dates. Ordinary two-way fixed-effects regressions may use already-treated groups as controls and assign nontransparent weights when effects vary, so the desired effect and comparison structure must be explicit.
major_error_concepts: Assuming one TWFE slope always equals the simple average post-treatment effect.
cards.prompt: What is Staggered Treatment Adoption? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Different adoption dates can create invalid or misleading weighted comparisons under heterogeneous effects.

cards.definition: A group-time treatment effect targets the effect for a specific adoption cohort at a specified date. Estimation can compare that cohort with suitable never-treated or not-yet-treated units under the appropriate parallel-trends and no-anticipation assumptions, then aggregate with explicit weights.
major_error_concepts: Averaging cohort effects without specifying which population and event-time weights are intended.
cards.prompt: What is Group Time Treatment Effect? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Cohort-and-date-specific effects with valid untreated comparisons and transparent aggregation.

cards.definition: Pretrend diagnostics examine observed pre-treatment differences or dynamics relevant to a parallel-trends argument. Low power, anticipatory behavior, and post-selection issues limit their interpretation; absence of a significant pretrend does not prove parallel counterfactual post-treatment trends.
major_error_concepts: Treating a passed pretrend test as automatic causal certification.
cards.prompt: What is Pretrend Diagnostics? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Preperiod evidence informs but does not establish the unobserved identifying trend assumption.

cards.definition: Regression discontinuity uses a treatment-assignment threshold in a running variable to identify a local effect under continuity or suitable local-randomization assumptions. The identification argument concerns behavior and outcomes near the cutoff, not comparisons of all units above and below it.
major_error_concepts: Assuming any arbitrary split at a chosen numeric value identifies a causal effect.
cards.prompt: What is Regression Discontinuity? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Threshold-based local comparison under an explicit identifying framework.

cards.definition: In sharp regression discontinuity, treatment changes deterministically at the cutoff. Under continuity of untreated and treated potential-outcome means and other design conditions, the outcome jump identifies the local treatment effect at that threshold.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting the cutoff effect automatically as an average effect far from the threshold.
cards.prompt: What is Sharp Regression Discontinuity? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Deterministic treatment jump plus potential-outcome continuity identifies a cutoff effect.

cards.definition: Fuzzy regression discontinuity allows the probability of treatment rather than treatment itself to jump at the cutoff. Under relevance, continuity, exclusion, and monotonicity conditions, the outcome jump divided by the treatment-probability jump identifies a local complier effect.
major_error_concepts: Dividing by a weak or zero treatment jump and claiming a precise global ATE.
cards.prompt: What is Fuzzy Regression Discontinuity? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Ratio of local outcome and treatment jumps under local IV assumptions.

accepted_variants: Cutoff bandwidth for local RD fitting.
cards.definition: An RD bandwidth selects the neighborhood around the threshold used for estimation. A narrower window can reduce approximation bias but raise variance; inference must account for smoothing bias through an appropriate procedure rather than simply selecting the visually nicest window.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the narrowest possible bandwidth always produces the most reliable estimate.
cards.prompt: What is RD Bandwidth? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Local window controls a bias-variance tradeoff and associated inference.

cards.definition: Sorting or manipulation near an RD cutoff can threaten continuity if units precisely choose which side of the threshold they occupy in outcome-relevant ways. Density and covariate diagnostics provide evidence but neither rejection nor non-rejection uniquely settles every design's validity.
major_error_concepts: Treating a density test alone as a complete proof or disproof of RD validity.
cards.prompt: What is RD Manipulation? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Precise outcome-related sorting can undermine local comparability.

cards.definition: A donut RD excludes observations very near the cutoff, often to address heaping or suspected manipulation. It removes direct near-threshold support and increases reliance on extrapolation across the excluded region, so it does not automatically restore identification.
major_error_concepts: Claiming deleting suspicious near-cutoff observations proves the remaining RD is unbiased.
cards.prompt: What is Donut Regression Discontinuity? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Exclude a cutoff neighborhood with added support and extrapolation consequences.

accepted_variants: Local linear RD as a common first-order case.
cards.definition: Local polynomial RD fits separate low-order smooth functions on either side of the cutoff and estimates their limit difference. Boundary behavior and smoothing bias matter, so flexible global high-order polynomials are not equivalent substitutes for justified local fitting and inference.
major_error_concepts: Assuming increasing a global polynomial degree necessarily improves cutoff identification.
cards.prompt: What is Local Polynomial RD? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Local side-specific approximation estimates the discontinuity with boundary-aware inference.

accepted_variants: Synthetic comparison unit with defined donor pool and weights.
cards.definition: Synthetic control constructs a weighted combination of comparison units to approximate a treated unit's pre-treatment trajectory or predictors. Post-treatment differences need assumptions about untreated evolution, donor contamination, and fit; the weighting algorithm alone does not identify the effect.
major_error_concepts: Assuming perfect pre-treatment fit guarantees the correct post-treatment counterfactual.
cards.prompt: What is Synthetic Control? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Weighted donor comparison aims to approximate a treated unit's untreated path.

accepted_variants: In-space or in-time placebo with interpretation specified.
cards.definition: Placebo analyses apply a treatment-like comparison where the hypothesized effect should be absent, such as untreated units or pre-treatment dates. They can reveal design weaknesses, but inferential comparisons require assumptions about comparability, assignment, and fit rather than informal rank counting alone.
major_error_concepts: Treating every placebo ranking as an exact randomization p-value without an assignment argument.
cards.prompt: What is Placebo Analysis? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Falsification comparison probes whether a design generates similar apparent effects elsewhere.

cards.definition: A treatment spillover occurs when one unit's treatment affects another unit's outcome. It can make untreated units inappropriate no-treatment controls and requires defining direct, indirect, or overall effects rather than silently assuming isolated treatment responses.
major_error_concepts: Calling an exposed untreated neighbor an unaffected control by treatment label alone.
cards.prompt: What is Treatment Spillovers? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Cross-unit treatment effects alter the counterfactual and effect definitions.

cards.definition: An exposure mapping summarizes which features of others' assignments matter for a unit's outcome, such as the treated share of its network. Identification relies on the mapping and assignment design; an incorrect summary can leave relevant interference unmodeled.
major_error_concepts: Assuming own treatment status is sufficient despite explicitly modeled network effects.
cards.prompt: What is Exposure Mapping? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Map assignment configurations to outcome-relevant exposure states.

cards.definition: Cluster randomization assigns treatment to groups rather than individuals. The estimand and inference must reflect the group-level assignment and possible within-group spillovers; adding individuals inside a fixed small set of groups does not create equally many independent assignment units.
major_error_concepts: Analyzing every individual as independently randomized when treatment was assigned by group.
cards.prompt: What is Cluster Randomized Design? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Group-level assignment determines randomization and uncertainty units.

cards.definition: A conditional average treatment effect is E[Y(1)-Y(0)|X=x] for specified pre-treatment covariates. Estimating heterogeneity requires the same identification foundations as average effects plus enough local information; searching many subgroups can overstate differences without honest inference.
major_error_concepts: Treating an estimated subgroup difference as an individual person's known treatment effect.
cards.prompt: What is Conditional Average Treatment Effect? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Average treatment contrast conditional on defined covariates.

cards.definition: Quantile regression models a conditional quantile of the outcome rather than its conditional mean. Coefficients describe covariate relationships at a specified conditional quantile under the model and do not automatically track the same individuals across outcome distributions.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting a quantile slope as the causal effect on people permanently ranked at that quantile.
cards.prompt: What is Quantile Regression? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Model a specified conditional outcome quantile.

cards.definition: The quantile check loss is rho_tau(u)=u*(tau-I[u<0]) for a quantile index tau between zero and one. Minimizing its expected value targets the corresponding quantile, and empirical minimization yields quantile estimators under appropriate design conditions.
major_error_concepts: Using symmetric squared loss while claiming it directly estimates any chosen quantile.
cards.prompt: What is Quantile Check Loss? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Asymmetric absolute loss targets the tau quantile.

accepted_variants: QTE with marginal or conditional target stated.
cards.definition: A quantile treatment effect contrasts quantiles of treated and untreated potential-outcome distributions. It generally differs from the quantile of individual treatment effects, which depends on the unobserved joint distribution of both potential outcomes.
major_error_concepts: Equating marginal quantile differences with individual rank-preserving gains without extra assumptions.
cards.prompt: What is Quantile Treatment Effect? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Difference of potential-outcome quantiles is not the quantile of individual differences.

accepted_variants: Poisson QMLE for a log-link conditional mean.
cards.definition: Poisson pseudo-maximum likelihood can estimate an exponential conditional mean when that mean is correctly specified, even without a Poisson conditional distribution under suitable regularity. Robust covariance addresses variance misspecification, but not an incorrect conditional mean or endogenous regressors.
major_error_concepts: Rejecting all PPML solely because conditional variance exceeds the mean.
cards.prompt: What is Poisson Pseudo Maximum Likelihood? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: PPML consistency can rely on correct mean rather than full Poisson variance assumptions.

accepted_variants: Poisson overdispersion when variance exceeds mean.
cards.definition: Overdispersion means conditional variance exceeds the benchmark variance, such as the mean in a Poisson model. It can motivate richer count distributions or robust inference, but its cause may include heterogeneity, dependence, or mean misspecification rather than one unique mechanism.
major_error_concepts: Treating overdispersion as proof that the conditional mean specification must be wrong.
cards.prompt: What is Count Data Overdispersion? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Conditional outcome variance exceeds the stated distributional benchmark.

accepted_variants: Two-part versus latent extra-zero count model.
cards.definition: A hurdle model separates the probability of a positive outcome from its conditional positive distribution, whereas a zero-inflated model mixes a special-zero process with a distribution that can itself generate zeros. The distinction is structural and must match the interpretation of zero observations.
major_error_concepts: Using the two model labels interchangeably without changing their zero probabilities.
cards.prompt: What is Hurdle and Zero Inflated Models? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Hurdle and zero-inflated models assign different mechanisms to zeros.

cards.definition: Duration analysis models the time until a defined event, accounting for timing, risk sets, and incomplete observation. The event definition and clock origin are part of the estimand; repeated or competing events require additional structure.
major_error_concepts: Treating an unobserved event time as necessarily an event occurring at follow-up end.
cards.prompt: What is Duration Analysis? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Time-to-event outcome with explicit event, origin, and observation process.

cards.definition: The hazard is the instantaneous event rate conditional on surviving event-free to that time. It is related to but differs from the survival probability; a larger hazard over a moment is not the same quantity as a larger cumulative event probability at a horizon.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting a hazard rate directly as a probability without an interval and conversion.
cards.prompt: What is Hazard Function? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Conditional instantaneous event rate among those still at risk.

accepted_variants: Among otherwise comparable units after conditioning on X, losing follow-up is unrelated to the latent event time; observed follow-up is the lesser of event and censoring times.
cards.definition: With event time T and censoring time C, right-censored data record min(T,C) and whether T<=C. A common independent-censoring assumption is T independent of C conditional on the modeled covariates X: within an X stratum, censoring time supplies no additional information about event time. This is stronger than merely labeling an observation censored; identifying survival over a target time range also needs a positive chance of remaining observed there.
major_error_concepts: Defining independent censoring solely as knowing the event occurs after a last observation.
Assuming dropout driven by unmeasured event risk is independent censoring.
Coding censoring time as an observed event time.
cards.prompt: What is conditionally independent right censoring in a time-to-event model? Distinguish the observation rule from the independence assumption.
required_concepts: State the right-censored observation min(T,C) and event indicator, or the equivalent event-free lower-bound interpretation.
Specify the conditional independence of event and censoring times given modeled covariates; right censoring alone does not imply this.

cards.definition: A Cox proportional-hazards model specifies h(t|X)=h0(t)*exp(X beta), leaving the baseline hazard unspecified. The proportional-hazards restriction makes covariate hazard ratios constant over time in that form; the coefficient is not directly a survival-probability difference.
major_error_concepts: Interpreting a hazard ratio as an equal ratio of survival probabilities at every horizon.
cards.prompt: What is Cox Proportional Hazards Model? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Multiplicative covariate effects on an unspecified baseline hazard.

accepted_variants: For an AR(1), the lag polynomial 1-rho L vanishes at L=1 when rho=1; with innovations the resulting process is a random walk, possibly with drift.
cards.definition: In y_t=c+rho*y_(t-1)+epsilon_t, an AR(1) has a unit root at one when rho=1. With IID mean-zero innovations of finite positive variance, independent of a finite-variance initial state, level shocks have permanent effects and the variance grows over time. Under that innovation law, a stable rho with absolute value below one can be very persistent, but its impulse effects decay and it admits a causal stationary solution. A deterministic trend alone is not a unit root. More generally, unit roots are roots of the autoregressive lag polynomial on the unit circle; the usual random-walk case is the root at one.
major_error_concepts: Equating rho=0.99 with an exact unit root.
Inferring a unit root solely from a visually trending sample.
cards.prompt: What is the unit root at +1 (the random-walk case) in an AR(1) process, and how does it differ from a stable coefficient near +1?
required_concepts: Identify rho=1 in the AR(1) random-walk case, not merely a coefficient close to one.
With the stated IID innovation law, unit-root level shocks do not decay as in a stable AR(1); deterministic trend and stochastic unit-root trend are distinct.

accepted_variants: ADF test with intercept and trend specification stated.
cards.definition: An augmented Dickey-Fuller test assesses a unit-root null using an autoregressive regression augmented with lagged differences. Critical values are nonstandard and depend on included deterministic terms; failure to reject can reflect limited power rather than confirmation of a unit root.
major_error_concepts: Using an ordinary regression t critical value for the unit-root coefficient test.
cards.prompt: What is Augmented Dickey Fuller Test? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Unit-root test with lagged-difference controls and appropriate nonstandard reference values.

accepted_variants: Cointegrating relation among I(1) variables in the standard case.
cards.definition: Cointegration means individually integrated variables have a nontrivial linear combination with a lower integration order, commonly stationary. It represents a persistent equilibrium-type relation under the model but does not on its own establish a causal direction.
major_error_concepts: Equating high correlation of trending levels with cointegration.
cards.prompt: What is Cointegration? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Nonstationary series can share a stationary linear combination.

cards.definition: An error-correction model includes lagged deviations from a cointegrating relation along with short-run changes. The adjustment coefficient describes response to disequilibrium under the model, while direction and causal interpretation require separate identifying assumptions.
major_error_concepts: Treating an error-correction term as an ordinary residual with no dynamic role.
cards.prompt: What is Error Correction Model? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Short-run dynamics respond to the previous long-run-equilibrium deviation.

cards.definition: A vector autoregression models several time-series variables using their own and each other's lags. Reduced-form innovations can be correlated, so their impulse responses are not uniquely interpretable as structural causal shocks without additional restrictions.
major_error_concepts: Calling each correlated equation residual an independently identified economic shock.
cards.prompt: What is Vector Autoregression? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Joint lagged linear dynamics do not by themselves identify structural shocks.

accepted_variants: SVAR identification with its restriction scheme stated.
cards.definition: Structural VAR identification maps reduced-form innovations into economically interpreted shocks using additional restrictions, such as timing, long-run effects, signs, or external instruments. Different restrictions can yield different identified sets or impulse responses from the same reduced-form fit.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a recursive variable ordering is a neutral assumption-free identification choice.
cards.prompt: What is Structural VAR Identification? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Additional economic restrictions distinguish structural disturbances from reduced-form innovations.

cards.definition: Local projections estimate separate regressions for outcomes at successive horizons to trace a shock's dynamic response. They still need a valid shock-identification argument and dependence-aware inference; flexible horizon-by-horizon estimation does not make a regressor exogenous.
major_error_concepts: Claiming local projections automatically eliminate endogeneity of the proposed shock.
cards.prompt: What is Local Projections? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Separate horizon regressions estimate dynamic responses conditional on identified shocks.

accepted_variants: Long-run variance or spectral-density-at-zero estimation under conventions.
cards.definition: Long-run covariance estimation includes contemporaneous and lagged covariance contributions needed for inference with serially dependent estimating functions. HAC bandwidth and kernel choices affect estimation, and the required covariance concerns the score or moment process, not merely raw outcome autocorrelation.
major_error_concepts: Computing only contemporaneous residual variance when score dependence persists over time.
cards.prompt: What is Long Run Covariance? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Covariance across lags of the relevant estimating process determines dependent-data uncertainty.

cards.definition: A pseudo-out-of-sample forecast exercise repeatedly fits using information available up to each forecast origin and evaluates later outcomes. Parameter selection, data availability, revisions, and overlapping horizons must be handled consistently with the claimed real-time prediction task.
major_error_concepts: Using future revised inputs and claiming the exercise reproduces historical real-time forecasts.
cards.prompt: What is Pseudo Out of Sample Forecasting? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Forecast evaluation respects historical information sets and timing.

cards.definition: Data vintages record which values were available at a particular release date before later revisions. Real-time econometric analysis must distinguish observation dates from release dates and revised values, since future information can leak into apparently historical predictions.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a past-dated observation necessarily had its current revised value known at that time.
cards.prompt: What is Real Time Data Vintages? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Vintage and release timing define the actual historical information set.

accepted_variants: Specification search and selective reporting concerns.
cards.definition: Researcher degrees of freedom include choices of outcomes, samples, transformations, models, and stopping rules made after inspecting results. Transparent specification histories, pre-specified tests where appropriate, and suitable multiplicity handling help separate confirmatory evidence from exploratory findings.
major_error_concepts: Presenting the best result from many tried analyses as a single pre-specified test.
cards.prompt: What is Researcher Degrees of Freedom? State its defining idea and essential conditions.
required_concepts: Data-dependent analytical choices affect nominal inference and must be disclosed or accounted for.
